public_rationale: At the May 16, 2023 Senate hearing, Altman said, “I have no equity in OpenAI,” without mentioning an indirect interest [e1]. An OpenAI page preserved on May 17, 2023 described his lack of direct equity and his indirect interest through a Y Combinator investment fund [e2]. TechCrunch reported on May 13, 2026 that Altman acknowledged this economic exposure and said he had not mentioned it in his Senate testimony [e3]. Together, these sources support the factual claim that his hearing answer omitted an indirect economic interest [e1][e2][e3].
limitations: Whether the interest should have been disclosed is a normative judgment; this assessment does not establish a legal disclosure duty, intent to deceive, or perjury.
The May 17, 2023 archive establishes the company disclosure's availability by that date, not its original publication date [e2].
The packet lacks underlying fund ownership documents and an official trial transcript. The historical ownership finding relies partly on retrospective reporting [e3].
The cited evidence does not establish the interest's value or ownership percentage.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Altman's Senate statement that he had no equity in OpenAI was only half true, because he held an indirect stake in OpenAI that should have been disclosed.

statement.excerpt: After poking around, I found out that “I have no equity in OpenAI” was only half the truth; while Altman to my knowledge holds no direct equity in OpenAI, he does have an indirect stake in OpenAI, and that fact should have been disclosed.

from_speaker: “I have no equity in OpenAI” was only half the truth
holds no direct equity in OpenAI
he does have an indirect stake in OpenAI
that fact should have been disclosed
our_interpretation: The factual test concerns Altman's ownership when he testified on May 16, 2023, because that exchange supplies the context for the alleged omission.
The ordinary reading of 'indirect stake' includes an economic interest through an investment fund holding OpenAI equity.
'Only half the truth' means that the answer omitted an indirect economic interest; it does not mean that exactly half of a numerical statement was false.
'Should have been disclosed' is treated as Marcus's judgment about completeness. This assessment does not determine a legal disclosure duty, intent to deceive, or perjury.
This is a qualitative claim about an individual's ownership. No company financial amount or valuation is being assessed, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: The hearing record shows the unqualified no-equity answer without mention of an indirect holding, and reliable evidence establishes that Altman then had an economic interest through a fund invested in OpenAI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable ownership evidence establishes that Altman had no indirect economic interest at the hearing, or the cited exchange actually disclosed that interest.
